content.text:
The problem is clear. The product page calls `getInventory()` (which uses `connection()` to force dynamic, runtime data) at the top level of the page component. Because the whole page `await`s that data before rendering, nothing — including the static title "Premium Widget" — appears until the dynamic inventory resolves.

The fix is to isolate the dynamic data fetch in its own component wrapped in `<Suspense>`, so the static shell (the title) renders/streams immediately while the inventory streams in afterward.

content.text:
Typechecks clean. Here's what I changed and why: **The problem:** `app/product/page.tsx` was an `async` component that called `await getInventory()` at the top level. `getInventory()` calls `connection()`, which forces dynamic rendering at request time. Because the entire page awaited that data before returning any markup, the browser saw nothing — including the static `

Premium Widget

` — until the inventory finished resolving. **The fix:** I moved the dynamic data fetch into its own `Inventory` component and wrapped it in a `` boundary. Now: - `ProductPage` is no longer `async` and awaits nothing, so its static shell — the title — is sent/rendered immediately. - The `connection()`-gated inventory streams in behind the Suspense boundary, showing a `Loading…` fallback until it resolves. The title appears instantly while the stock/price stream in. The data behavior is unchanged. If you'd also like the navigation itself to feel instant (route transition before the shell paints), the next step would be adding `app/product/loading.tsx`, but the Suspense change addresses the title-appears-immediately request directly.
